en: My phone battery drains very fast these days.
tamil: இப்பல்லாம் என் போன் பேட்டரி ரொம்ப சீக்கிரம் தீர்ந்துடுது.
context: Complaining about a weak phone battery.
explain: Present simple shows a regular habit or problem. 'These days' means recently.
usage: Say it to a friend or at a mobile shop when your phone needs repair.
leelaQ: How is your phone battery these days?
answer: My phone battery is good, but it needs charging twice a day.

en: I forgot my Wi-Fi password again.
tamil: நான் மறுபடியும் என் வைஃபை பாஸ்வேர்டை மறந்துட்டேன்.
context: Telling a family member you forgot the Wi-Fi password.
explain: 'Forgot' is the past of 'forget'. 'Again' shows it has happened before.
usage: Use it at home when you cannot connect a device to the internet.
leelaQ: Do you remember all your passwords?
answer: No, I forget them often, so I write them in a notebook.

en: The video call is not clear because the internet is slow.
tamil: இன்டர்நெட் ஸ்லோவா இருக்கறதால வீடியோ கால் தெளிவா இல்ல.
context: Explaining a bad video call to a colleague.
explain: 'Because' gives the reason. 'Is not' makes the sentence negative.
usage: Say it in an online meeting when others cannot hear or see you well.
leelaQ: What do you do when the internet is slow?
answer: I restart the router and wait for a few minutes.

en: I will send you the file on WhatsApp in five minutes.
tamil: நான் அஞ்சு நிமிஷத்துல உனக்கு ஃபைலை வாட்ஸ்அப்ல அனுப்புறேன்.
context: Promising to share a file with a friend.
explain: 'Will' shows a promise about the future. 'In five minutes' tells when.
usage: Use it with friends or coworkers who are waiting for a document.
leelaQ: How do you share photos with your family?
answer: I send them on WhatsApp because everyone uses it.

en: Please turn off your mic when you are not speaking.
tamil: நீங்க பேசாதப்போ தயவுசெஞ்சு உங்க மைக்கை ஆஃப் பண்ணுங்க.
context: Asking participants in an online meeting to mute.
explain: 'Please' makes an order polite. 'When' joins two ideas about time.
usage: A meeting host can say this when there is background noise.
leelaQ: Have you ever attended an online meeting?
answer: Yes, I attended one last week with my team.

en: My laptop is hanging, so I cannot finish my work.
tamil: என் லேப்டாப் ஹேங் ஆகுது, அதனால என் வேலையை முடிக்க முடியல.
context: Telling your manager about a computer problem.
explain: 'So' shows the result. 'Cannot' means you are not able to do something.
usage: Use it at the office when a computer problem delays your work.
leelaQ: What do you do when your laptop hangs?
answer: I close extra apps and restart it.

en: Could you share your screen so that we can see the slides?
tamil: நாங்க ஸ்லைடுகளைப் பார்க்க உங்க ஸ்கிரீனை ஷேர் பண்ண முடியுமா?
context: Asking a presenter in an online meeting.
explain: 'Could you' is a polite request. 'So that' gives the purpose.
usage: Use it in a video meeting when someone is explaining something.
leelaQ: How do you present your ideas in a meeting?
answer: I make simple slides and explain them slowly.

en: I have already updated the app, but it still crashes.
tamil: நான் ஆப்பை ஏற்கனவே அப்டேட் பண்ணிட்டேன், ஆனாலும் அது க்ராஷ் ஆகுது.
context: Reporting an app problem to customer support.
explain: 'Have updated' shows an action that is finished but matters now. 'Still' shows the problem continues.
usage: Say it to customer support when an app does not work properly.
leelaQ: Which app do you use the most?
answer: I use WhatsApp the most, for chatting and calling.

en: Never share your OTP with anyone.
tamil: உன் ஓடிபியை யார்கிட்டயும் ஷேர் பண்ணாதே.
context: Warning a family member about online fraud.
explain: 'Never' makes a strong negative order. An OTP is a secret code for safe payments.
usage: Say it to parents or friends to keep them safe from online cheating.
leelaQ: How can we stay safe from online fraud?
answer: We should never share our OTP or bank details with anyone.

en: She is posting photos of her trip on Instagram.
tamil: அவ தன்னோட டிரிப் போட்டோக்களை இன்ஸ்டாகிராம்ல போஸ்ட் பண்ணிட்டு இருக்கா.
context: Telling a friend what someone is doing right now.
explain: Present continuous shows an action happening now. Use 'is' with he, she and it.
usage: Use it when you see a friend's or relative's activity on social media.
leelaQ: Do you post photos on social media?
answer: Yes, I post a few photos when I go to new places.

en: My phone fell down and the screen is cracked.
tamil: என் போன் கீழ விழுந்து ஸ்கிரீன் உடைஞ்சிடுச்சு.
context: Telling a shop owner about a broken phone.
explain: 'Fell' is the past of 'fall'. 'Is cracked' describes the present condition.
usage: Say it at a mobile repair shop to explain the damage.
leelaQ: Has your phone ever fallen and broken?
answer: Yes, it fell from the table once and the screen cracked.

en: Where can I charge my phone?
tamil: என் போனை எங்க சார்ஜ் பண்ணலாம்?
context: Asking for a charging point at a railway station.
explain: 'Where can I...?' asks about a place where something is possible.
usage: Ask at a station, cafe or office when your battery is low.
leelaQ: Where do you usually charge your phone?
answer: I charge it near my bed every night.

en: Can you hear me properly?
tamil: நான் பேசுறது உனக்கு நல்லா கேக்குதா?
context: Checking audio at the start of a call.
explain: 'Can you hear me?' is the standard check at the start of a call. 'Properly' means well.
usage: Use it at the start of a phone or video call.
leelaQ: What do you check before a video call starts?
answer: I check my camera, my mic and my internet.

en: I am going to install a new keyboard app.
tamil: நான் ஒரு புது கீபோர்டு ஆப்பை இன்ஸ்டால் பண்ணப் போறேன்.
context: Telling a friend about a phone plan.
explain: 'Going to' talks about a plan you already made.
usage: Say it when you want to try a new app on your phone.
leelaQ: What new app are you going to try?
answer: I am going to try a language learning app.

en: The meeting link is not working for me.
tamil: மீட்டிங் லிங்க் எனக்கு வேலை செய்யல.
context: Telling the organiser the link does not open.
explain: 'Not working' is a common way to say something does not function.
usage: Message the organiser when you cannot join an online meeting.
leelaQ: What do you do if you cannot join a meeting?
answer: I ask the organiser to send the link again.

en: Please send me the link again.
tamil: தயவுசெஞ்சு லிங்கை மறுபடியும் அனுப்புங்க.
context: Asking a colleague to resend a link.
explain: 'Again' means one more time. 'Please' keeps the request polite.
usage: Use it in chat when a link is lost or has expired.
leelaQ: Who sends you links most often?
answer: My brother sends me funny videos and links.

en: How do I change my profile picture?
tamil: என் ப்ரொஃபைல் படத்தை எப்படி மாத்துறது?
context: Asking a friend for help with an account.
explain: 'How do I...?' asks for steps to do something.
usage: Ask a friend or a helper when you use a new app.
leelaQ: What picture do you keep as your profile photo?
answer: I keep a simple photo of myself smiling.

en: I need to reset my password.
tamil: நான் என் பாஸ்வேர்டை ரீசெட் பண்ணணும்.
context: Telling IT support you are locked out.
explain: 'Need to' shows something necessary. 'Reset' means set again.
usage: Say it to the IT team or customer care when you cannot log in.
leelaQ: When did you last change a password?
answer: I changed my email password last month.

en: I have been using this laptop for five years.
tamil: நான் இந்த லேப்டாப்பை அஞ்சு வருஷமா யூஸ் பண்றேன்.
context: Telling a shop owner how old your laptop is.
explain: 'Have been using' with 'for' shows an action that started in the past and continues.
usage: Say it when you ask if an old device is worth repairing.
leelaQ: How long have you had your phone?
answer: I have had it for two years.

en: Let me check my internet connection.
tamil: நான் என் இன்டர்நெட் கனெக்ஷனை செக் பண்ணிப் பாக்குறேன்.
context: Saying this during a bad call.
explain: 'Let me' is a friendly way to offer to do something.
usage: Use it when a call is breaking and you want a moment to fix it.
leelaQ: What do you do when your call keeps cutting?
answer: I move near the window and call again.

en: Do you have a charger I can borrow?
tamil: நான் வாங்கிக்கிற மாதிரி உன்கிட்ட சார்ஜர் இருக்கா?
context: Asking a colleague for a phone charger.
explain: 'Do you have...?' asks if someone has something. 'I can borrow' tells why you ask.
usage: Ask at the office or in a bus station when your phone is dying.
leelaQ: Do you carry a power bank when you travel?
answer: Yes, I always carry a power bank in my bag.

en: He will join the call after lunch.
tamil: அவன் மதிய சாப்பாட்டுக்கு அப்புறம் கால்ல சேருவான்.
context: Telling the team about someone's availability.
explain: 'Will join' is a simple prediction or plan about the future.
usage: Say it when someone is absent from a meeting but will come later.
leelaQ: When will you join the next meeting?
answer: I will join it at ten o'clock tomorrow.

en: Sorry, I was on mute.
tamil: மன்னிக்கணும், நான் மியூட்ல இருந்தேன்.
context: Apologising in an online meeting.
explain: 'Was' is used with I, he, she and it. 'On mute' means the sound is off.
usage: A very common sentence in online meetings when nobody could hear you.
leelaQ: What happens when someone forgets to unmute?
answer: Everybody waits and says we cannot hear you.

en: My phone is out of storage.
tamil: என் போன்ல ஸ்டோரேஜ் முடிஞ்சிடுச்சு.
context: Complaining that you cannot save more photos.
explain: 'Out of' means there is none left.
usage: Say it when the phone gives a storage full message.
leelaQ: What takes the most space on your phone?
answer: Videos take the most space on my phone.

en: I deleted some old photos to free up space.
tamil: இடம் காலி பண்ண சில பழைய போட்டோக்களை டெலீட் பண்ணினேன்.
context: Explaining how you fixed the storage problem.
explain: 'To free up space' tells the purpose. 'To' plus a verb gives a reason.
usage: Use it when talking about cleaning your phone.
leelaQ: How do you keep your phone clean and fast?
answer: I delete old photos and unused apps every month.

en: The app asks for my location every time.
tamil: அந்த ஆப் ஒவ்வொரு தடவையும் என் லொகேஷனைக் கேக்குது.
context: Complaining about app permissions.
explain: 'Every time' shows something that happens again and again.
usage: Say it when an app wants too many permissions.
leelaQ: Do you allow apps to use your location?
answer: Only maps and delivery apps can use my location.

en: Please do not click on unknown links.
tamil: தெரியாத லிங்க்குகளை கிளிக் பண்ணாதீங்க.
context: Warning colleagues about phishing messages.
explain: 'Do not' plus a verb is a polite warning. 'Unknown' means not known.
usage: A manager or an IT person can say this to protect the team.
leelaQ: What would you do with a strange link in a message?
answer: I would not open it and I would delete the message.

en: I downloaded the invoice, but I cannot open it.
tamil: நான் இன்வாய்ஸை டவுன்லோட் பண்ணிட்டேன், ஆனா அதை திறக்க முடியல.
context: Telling accounts staff about a file problem.
explain: 'But' joins two opposite ideas.
usage: Say it at work when a document does not open.
leelaQ: What kind of files do you download most?
answer: I download PDF files like bills and tickets.

en: We are using a new software for billing.
tamil: நாங்க பில்லிங்குக்கு ஒரு புது சாஃப்ட்வேர் யூஸ் பண்றோம்.
context: Telling a customer about a change in the shop.
explain: Present continuous shows a current situation, not only this moment.
usage: Use it in a shop or office when systems are changing.
leelaQ: Does your workplace use any special software?
answer: Yes, we use software to track our orders.

en: The server is down, so the website will not open.
tamil: சர்வர் டவுன், அதனால வெப்சைட் ஓப்பன் ஆகாது.
context: Explaining why a website is not loading.
explain: 'Down' means not working. 'Will not' says what to expect.
usage: IT staff say this when customers cannot reach a site.
leelaQ: What do you do when a website does not open?
answer: I wait a little and try again.

en: I charged my phone all night, but it is still at ten percent.
tamil: நான் நைட் முழுக்க போனை சார்ஜ் பண்ணினேன், ஆனா இன்னும் பத்து சதவீதம்தான் இருக்கு.
context: Complaining to a repair shop about charging.
explain: 'All night' means for the whole night. 'Still' shows surprise.
usage: Say it to a technician when the charger or battery may be faulty.
leelaQ: How long does your phone take to charge?
answer: It takes about two hours to charge fully.

en: I have not received the OTP yet.
tamil: எனக்கு இன்னும் ஓடிபி வரல.
context: Telling customer care about a missing code.
explain: 'Have not received... yet' shows something expected has not happened.
usage: Say it on a bank or app helpline when a code does not come.
leelaQ: What do you do when an OTP does not come?
answer: I wait one minute and then press resend.

en: She is learning to edit videos on her phone.
tamil: அவ தன் போன்ல வீடியோ எடிட் பண்ணக் கத்துக்கிட்டு இருக்கா.
context: Telling a friend about a new hobby.
explain: 'Learning to' plus a verb says what someone is studying.
usage: Use it when talking about a person's new skill.
leelaQ: Would you like to make videos?
answer: Yes, I would like to make short cooking videos.

en: Our team meeting is scheduled for ten o'clock.
tamil: எங்க டீம் மீட்டிங் பத்து மணிக்கு ஷெட்யூல் ஆகியிருக்கு.
context: Reminding a colleague about a meeting.
explain: 'Is scheduled for' means a time has been fixed.
usage: Use it in office chats to confirm the time of a meeting.
leelaQ: What time is your next meeting?
answer: My next meeting is at three o'clock this afternoon.

en: I will call you back after I finish this online class.
tamil: இந்த ஆன்லைன் கிளாஸ் முடிச்சதும் நான் உன்னைத் திருப்பிக் கூப்பிடுறேன்.
context: Telling a friend you cannot talk now.
explain: 'Call back' means call someone again. After 'after', use present simple.
usage: Say it when you are busy but want to speak later.
leelaQ: What do you say when you cannot take a call?
answer: I say I am busy and I will call back soon.

en: My email got hacked last week.
tamil: போன வாரம் என் மெயில் ஹேக் ஆயிடுச்சு.
context: Telling a friend about an account problem.
explain: 'Got hacked' means someone broke into the account.
usage: Say it when you warn people about strange messages from your account.
leelaQ: What can we do to protect our accounts?
answer: We can use strong passwords and two-step login.

en: You should turn on two-step verification.
tamil: நீ டூ-ஸ்டெப் வெரிஃபிகேஷனை ஆன் பண்ணணும்.
context: Advising a friend about account safety.
explain: 'Should' gives advice. Two-step verification adds a second check.
usage: Use it to advise family and friends who use online banking.
leelaQ: Do you use two-step verification?
answer: Yes, I use it for my email and my bank app.

en: The new phone has a very good camera.
tamil: புது போன்ல கேமரா ரொம்ப நல்லா இருக்கு.
context: Praising a phone you are thinking of buying.
explain: 'Has' is used with he, she and it for possession.
usage: Say it while talking about a phone at a shop or with friends.
leelaQ: What do you look for when you buy a phone?
answer: I look for good battery life and a clear camera.

en: I bought these earphones online last week.
tamil: நான் இந்த இயர்ஃபோன்களை போன வாரம் ஆன்லைன்ல வாங்கினேன்.
context: Telling a friend where you got something.
explain: 'Last week' is a time word for the simple past.
usage: Use it in casual talk about shopping for gadgets.
leelaQ: Do you shop online?
answer: Yes, I shop online for clothes and books.

en: The screen is too bright, so I am changing the settings.
tamil: ஸ்கிரீன் ரொம்ப பிரைட்டா இருக்கு, அதனால நான் செட்டிங்ஸை மாத்துறேன்.
context: Explaining what you are doing on a device.
explain: 'Too' means more than needed. 'So' shows the result.
usage: Say it when adjusting your phone in a dark place.
leelaQ: Do you use your phone at night?
answer: Yes, I use it at night with a low brightness.

en: I usually watch tutorials on YouTube to learn new things.
tamil: புது விஷயங்கள் கத்துக்க நான் பொதுவா யூடியூப்ல டுடோரியல்ஸ் பாப்பேன்.
context: Talking about how you learn online.
explain: 'Usually' is a frequency word for habits. 'To learn' shows purpose.
usage: Use it when someone asks how you learned a skill.
leelaQ: What have you learned from YouTube?
answer: I learned how to cook and fix small things at home.

en: Our printer is jammed again.
tamil: எங்க பிரிண்டர்ல பேப்பர் மறுபடியும் சிக்கிடுச்சு.
context: Telling the office that the printer is not working.
explain: 'Jammed' means stuck. 'Again' shows it happens often.
usage: Say it in the office when you want help with a printer.
leelaQ: How often do you print documents?
answer: I print documents once or twice a week.

en: My friend helped me to set up my new smartphone.
tamil: என் நண்பன் என் புது ஸ்மார்ட்போனை செட் பண்ண உதவினான்.
context: Telling someone who helped you with a gadget.
explain: 'Help someone to do' is a common pattern. 'Set up' means get ready to use.
usage: Use it to thank or mention a person who helped with tech.
leelaQ: Who helps you when you have a tech problem?
answer: My younger brother helps me because he knows a lot.

en: I will be offline for an hour because of a power cut.
tamil: கரண்ட் கட் ஆனதால நான் ஒரு மணி நேரம் ஆஃப்லைன்ல இருப்பேன்.
context: Informing your team about no electricity.
explain: 'Will be' talks about a future state. 'Because of' is followed by a noun.
usage: Send it to your team when you expect a power or internet cut.
leelaQ: What do you do during a power cut?
answer: I read a book or talk with my family.

en: The online class starts at six, so please be on time.
tamil: ஆன்லைன் கிளாஸ் ஆறு மணிக்குத் தொடங்கும், அதனால தயவுசெஞ்சு சரியான நேரத்துக்கு வாங்க.
context: A teacher reminding students.
explain: Present simple is used for fixed timetables. 'On time' means not late.
usage: A teacher or organiser can say this in a group chat.
leelaQ: Have you attended any online class?
answer: Yes, I attended an English class online.

en: I saved the document in a folder on my desktop.
tamil: நான் டாக்குமெண்டை என் டெஸ்க்டாப்ல ஒரு ஃபோல்டர்ல சேவ் பண்ணினேன்.
context: Telling a colleague where a file is.
explain: 'In' shows the folder and 'on' the desktop screen.
usage: Say it when someone asks where you kept a file.
leelaQ: How do you keep your files organised?
answer: I keep them in folders with clear names.

en: Please connect to the office Wi-Fi to download the update.
tamil: அப்டேட்டை டவுன்லோட் பண்ண ஆஃபீஸ் வைஃபையில கனெக்ட் ஆகுங்க.
context: Advising a coworker.
explain: 'To download' gives the reason. 'Please' keeps it polite.
usage: Use it when a large file should not use mobile data.
leelaQ: When do you use mobile data?
answer: I use it when I am outside and there is no Wi-Fi.

en: It is a good idea to back up your photos.
tamil: உன் போட்டோக்களை பேக்அப் எடுத்து வைக்கிறது நல்லது.
context: Advising a friend before changing phones.
explain: 'It is a good idea to' plus a verb gives friendly advice.
usage: Say it to someone who may lose data when a phone is lost.
leelaQ: Have you ever lost important data?
answer: Yes, I lost some photos once, so now I make backups.

en: My grandmother is learning to make video calls.
tamil: என் பாட்டி வீடியோ கால் பண்ணக் கத்துக்கிட்டு இருக்காங்க.
context: Talking about a family member and new technology.
explain: 'Is learning' shows she is in the middle of learning.
usage: Use it in a casual chat about family and gadgets.
leelaQ: How do older people in your family use technology?
answer: My parents use WhatsApp to see photos and talk to us.

en: I have already logged out of all my accounts.
tamil: நான் என் எல்லா அக்கவுண்ட்டுலயும் ஏற்கனவே லாக் அவுட் பண்ணிட்டேன்.
context: Telling someone that you are safe after a problem.
explain: 'Already' shows something was done earlier than expected.
usage: Use it after a phone is lost or a security warning comes.
leelaQ: What do you do if you lose your phone?
answer: I lock it from another device and call my SIM provider.

en: This app is easy to use even for beginners.
tamil: இந்த ஆப்பை ஆரம்பிக்கிறவங்களும் ஈஸியா யூஸ் பண்ணலாம்.
context: Recommending an app to a friend.
explain: 'Easy to use' describes a simple tool. 'Even for' adds a surprise.
usage: Say it when you suggest an app to someone new to technology.
leelaQ: Which app would you suggest to a beginner?
answer: I would suggest a simple app like WhatsApp.

en: The phone was on silent, so I missed your call.
tamil: போன் சைலண்ட்ல இருந்துச்சு, அதனால உன் கால் மிஸ் ஆயிடுச்சு.
context: Apologising for a missed call.
explain: 'Missed' is the past of 'miss'. 'So' gives the result.
usage: Say it to friends or family when they are upset about a call.
leelaQ: Do you keep your phone on silent?
answer: Only in meetings, otherwise I keep it on loud.

en: I forgot to attach the file to the email.
tamil: நான் மெயில்ல ஃபைலை அட்டாச் பண்ண மறந்துட்டேன்.
context: Admitting a common email mistake.
explain: 'Forgot to' plus a verb means you did not do something you should have done.
usage: Say it at work before sending a second email.
leelaQ: What mistakes do you make in emails?
answer: I sometimes forget the attachment or the subject.

en: My neighbour is fixing my TV remote.
tamil: என் பக்கத்து வீட்டுக்காரர் என் டிவி ரிமோட்டை சரிசெய்றாங்க.
context: Telling a visitor what is happening.
explain: Present continuous is used for something happening now.
usage: Use it in casual talk about gadgets at home.
leelaQ: Can you fix small things at home?
answer: Yes, I can fix a switch or change a bulb.

en: I am not comfortable sharing my phone number online.
tamil: என் போன் நம்பரை ஆன்லைன்ல பகிர எனக்கு வசதியா இல்ல.
context: Refusing to give personal details.
explain: 'Comfortable doing' shows how you feel. 'Not' makes it negative.
usage: Say it when a website or a stranger asks for personal details.
leelaQ: What information should we not share online?
answer: We should not share passwords or our home address.

en: Do not forget to charge your laptop before the meeting.
tamil: மீட்டிங்குக்கு முன்னாடி உன் லேப்டாப்பை சார்ஜ் பண்ண மறந்துடாதே.
context: Reminding a colleague.
explain: 'Do not forget to' plus a verb is a friendly reminder.
usage: Use it before a long meeting or a trip.
leelaQ: What do you do before an important meeting?
answer: I charge my laptop and test my camera.

en: I don't use social media during exam time.
tamil: நான் தேர்வு நேரத்துல சோஷியல் மீடியா யூஸ் பண்றதில்ல.
context: Explaining a good habit to a friend.
explain: 'Don't' makes present simple negative with I, you, we and they.
usage: Say it when talking about focus and study habits.
leelaQ: Does social media waste your time?
answer: Sometimes it does, so I limit it to thirty minutes a day.

en: Hello, can everyone see my screen?
tamil: ஹலோ, எல்லாருக்கும் என் ஸ்கிரீன் தெரியுதா?
context: Starting a presentation online.
explain: 'Can everyone...?' checks with a group. It is a common meeting phrase.
usage: Say it just after you start sharing your screen.
leelaQ: What do you say at the start of a presentation?
answer: I say hello and ask if everyone can hear me.

en: Which phone is better for a small budget?
tamil: சின்ன பட்ஜெட்டுக்கு எந்த போன் நல்லது?
context: Asking a salesperson for advice.
explain: 'Which' is used when choosing from a few options.
usage: Ask at a mobile shop or from a friend who knows phones.
leelaQ: What is a good budget for a phone?
answer: About fifteen thousand rupees is a good budget for me.

en: How much data do I have left?
tamil: எனக்கு எவ்வளவு டேட்டா மீதி இருக்கு?
context: Checking your mobile plan.
explain: 'How much' is used for things we cannot count, like data.
usage: Ask at a mobile store or in an app at the end of the month.
leelaQ: How much data do you use every day?
answer: I use about two GB every day.

en: When did the update finish?
tamil: அப்டேட் எப்போ முடிஞ்சுது?
context: Asking an IT colleague.
explain: 'When did' asks about the time of a past event. After 'did', use the base verb.
usage: Use it in the office when a system was down for maintenance.
leelaQ: What do you do while an update is running?
answer: I drink tea and wait.

en: Why is my phone getting so hot?
tamil: என் போன் ஏன் இவ்வளவு சூடாகுது?
context: Asking a technician about overheating.
explain: 'Why' asks for a reason. 'Getting hot' shows a change.
usage: Ask a technician or a friend when your phone overheats.
leelaQ: What makes a phone hot?
answer: Playing games for a long time makes it hot.

en: Are you free for a quick video call?
tamil: உனக்கு ஒரு சின்ன வீடியோ கால் பண்ண நேரம் இருக்கா?
context: Asking a colleague for a short call.
explain: 'Are you free?' asks if someone has time.
usage: Use it with coworkers before you call them.
leelaQ: When do you prefer to have calls?
answer: I prefer calls in the evening after work.

en: Who is hosting the meeting today?
tamil: இன்னைக்கு மீட்டிங்கை யார் ஹோஸ்ட் பண்றாங்க?
context: Asking about the organiser.
explain: 'Hosting' means running the meeting.
usage: Ask it when you cannot find the link.
leelaQ: Who usually leads your meetings?
answer: My manager usually leads them.

en: Did you see the message in the group?
tamil: க்ரூப்ல வந்த மெசேஜை பாத்தியா?
context: Asking a friend about a group chat.
explain: 'Did you see...?' asks about a past action.
usage: Ask classmates or coworkers about news in a group chat.
leelaQ: Are you in many WhatsApp groups?
answer: Yes, I am in about ten groups.

en: What is the Wi-Fi name and password?
tamil: வைஃபை பேரு என்ன, பாஸ்வேர்டு என்ன?
context: Asking at a cafe or a friend's house.
explain: Wi-Fi names are called SSIDs, but people simply say 'Wi-Fi name'.
usage: A very common question when you visit a place and need the internet.
leelaQ: Where do you ask for the Wi-Fi password?
answer: I ask the staff at a cafe or my friend at home.

en: Will the app work without internet?
tamil: இன்டர்நெட் இல்லாம இந்த ஆப் வேலை செய்யுமா?
context: Asking about an app feature.
explain: 'Will' asks about the future. 'Without' means not having.
usage: Ask before you travel to a place with weak signal.
leelaQ: Which apps do you use offline?
answer: I use music and notes apps offline.

en: Is it safe to pay through this link?
tamil: இந்த லிங்க் வழியா பணம் கட்டுறது பாதுகாப்பானதா?
context: Checking before an online payment.
explain: 'Is it safe to...?' asks about safety.
usage: Ask a family member or a bank when you are not sure about a payment.
leelaQ: How do you pay for things online?
answer: I pay with UPI because it is quick and simple.

en: Have you tried turning it off and on again?
tamil: நீ அதை ஆஃப் பண்ணிட்டு திரும்ப ஆன் பண்ணிப் பாத்தியா?
context: The classic tech support advice.
explain: 'Have you tried...?' asks about experience. It uses the -ing form after 'tried'.
usage: Help desk staff say this first for almost every problem.
leelaQ: What is your first step when a device does not work?
answer: I restart it and check the cables.

en: Could you speak a little louder? The sound is low.
tamil: கொஞ்சம் சத்தமா பேச முடியுமா? சவுண்ட் கம்மியா இருக்கு.
context: Asking a speaker in an online meeting.
explain: 'A little louder' makes the request soft. The second sentence gives the reason.
usage: Use it when you cannot hear someone on a call.
leelaQ: Do you speak clearly on calls?
answer: I try to speak slowly and clearly.

en: Please help me to download this app.
tamil: இந்த ஆப்பை டவுன்லோட் பண்ண எனக்கு உதவி பண்ணுங்க.
context: Asking a younger person for help.
explain: 'Help me to' plus a verb is polite when you say 'please'.
usage: Say it to a child or a friend who is good with technology.
leelaQ: Who do you ask for help with apps?
answer: I ask my nephew because he knows many apps.

en: Could you put the link in the chat box?
tamil: லிங்கை சாட் பாக்ஸ்ல போட முடியுமா?
context: Asking in an online meeting.
explain: 'Could you put...' is polite. 'Chat box' is the area for messages in a call.
usage: Use it in a video call when a speaker mentions a link.
leelaQ: What do people usually write in the chat box?
answer: They write questions and links.

en: Please switch on your camera for a minute.
tamil: தயவுசெஞ்சு ஒரு நிமிஷம் உங்க கேமராவை ஆன் பண்ணுங்க.
context: A teacher asking students.
explain: 'Switch on' is the same as 'turn on'.
usage: A teacher or an interviewer says this during an online session.
leelaQ: Do you like to keep your camera on?
answer: Not always, but I keep it on in interviews.

en: Can you teach me how to use Excel?
tamil: எக்ஸெல்லை எப்படி யூஸ் பண்றதுன்னு எனக்கு சொல்லித் தர முடியுமா?
context: Asking a coworker.
explain: 'How to' plus a verb asks for a method.
usage: Ask a colleague when you must learn a new office tool.
leelaQ: What computer skill do you want to learn?
answer: I want to learn Excel for my work.

en: Please speak slowly, the network is breaking.
tamil: தயவுசெஞ்சு மெதுவா பேசுங்க, நெட்வொர்க் கட் ஆகுது.
context: Asking on a poor line.
explain: 'Breaking' means the signal is cutting in and out.
usage: Say it on a phone call when the signal is weak.
leelaQ: Where is your phone signal weak?
answer: The signal is weak in our basement.

en: Could you please resend the invoice in PDF?
tamil: இன்வாய்ஸை PDF-ல திருப்பி அனுப்ப முடியுமா?
context: Asking a vendor by email.
explain: 'Resend' means send again. 'In PDF' means in that file format.
usage: Use it in formal emails with clients and vendors.
leelaQ: What file formats do you know?
answer: I know PDF, Word and Excel.

en: Please keep your phone away from the exam hall.
tamil: தயவுசெஞ்சு உங்க போனை தேர்வு அறைக்கு வெளியில வெச்சிடுங்க.
context: A supervisor's instruction.
explain: 'Keep away from' means do not bring near.
usage: A rule said in schools, colleges and offices.
leelaQ: Where do you keep your phone while studying?
answer: I keep it in another room.

en: Excuse me, how do I connect to this printer?
tamil: மன்னிக்கணும், இந்த பிரிண்டர்ல எப்படி கனெக்ட் பண்றது?
context: Asking office staff.
explain: 'Excuse me' starts a polite question.
usage: Use it in a new office or a shop.
leelaQ: What do you print at work?
answer: I print reports and tickets.

en: I do not understand how this app works.
tamil: இந்த ஆப் எப்படி வேலை செய்யுதுன்னு எனக்கு புரியல.
context: Asking for help.
explain: 'How this app works' is a noun clause: the word order is like a statement.
usage: Say it to a helper or in a review when an app is confusing.
leelaQ: What do you do when you cannot use a new app?
answer: I watch a short video or ask a friend.

en: He never turns off his notifications, so his phone keeps buzzing.
tamil: அவன் நோட்டிபிகேஷன்களை ஆஃப் பண்ணவே மாட்டான், அதனால அவன் போன் அடிச்சுக்கிட்டே இருக்கும்.
context: Talking about a friend.
explain: 'Never' is a frequency word with a negative meaning.
usage: Use it jokingly about a friend who is always on the phone.
leelaQ: Do you get many notifications?
answer: Yes, I get too many, so I turned off some.

en: I did not know that you can mute a chat group.
tamil: க்ரூப் சாட்டை மியூட் பண்ணலாம்னு எனக்குத் தெரியாது.
context: Learning a tip from a friend.
explain: 'Did not know' is the past negative.
usage: Say it when someone teaches you a new phone tip.
leelaQ: What new phone tip did you learn recently?
answer: I learned how to scan documents with my phone.

en: My phone does not turn on after the update.
tamil: அப்டேட் பண்ணின பிறகு என் போன் ஆன் ஆகல.
context: Reporting a problem at a service centre.
explain: 'Does not' is used with he, she and it.
usage: Say it at a service centre when a phone stops working.
leelaQ: What would you do if your phone does not turn on?
answer: I would charge it and then take it to a service centre.

en: I can't log in because the system says my password is wrong.
tamil: நான் லாக் இன் பண்ண முடியல, ஏன்னா என் பாஸ்வேர்டு தப்புன்னு சிஸ்டம் சொல்லுது.
context: Telling IT support.
explain: 'Can't' is the short form of 'cannot'.
usage: Say it to the IT team in an office.
leelaQ: Do you use the same password everywhere?
answer: No, I use different passwords for different sites.

en: No, I have not downloaded that app.
tamil: இல்ல, நான் அந்த ஆப்பை டவுன்லோட் பண்ணல.
context: Answering a friend's question.
explain: A short negative answer can start with 'No'.
usage: Use it as a clear, polite answer in a conversation.
leelaQ: Which apps have you not tried yet?
answer: I have not tried any food delivery app yet.

en: The meeting will not start until everyone joins.
tamil: எல்லாரும் வர்ற வரைக்கும் மீட்டிங் தொடங்காது.
context: Informing participants.
explain: 'Until' means up to the time that something happens.
usage: A host says it when people are still waiting.
leelaQ: What do you do while waiting for a meeting?
answer: I check my emails or talk to colleagues.

en: I will not use my phone while driving.
tamil: நான் வண்டி ஓட்டும்போது போன் யூஸ் பண்ண மாட்டேன்.
context: Making a promise about safety.
explain: 'Will not' makes a firm promise. 'While driving' shows two actions together.
usage: Say it to family to show you follow road safety.
leelaQ: Why should we not use phones while driving?
answer: It is dangerous and can cause accidents.

en: Our website is not secure, so we are fixing it now.
tamil: எங்க வெப்சைட் பாதுகாப்பா இல்ல, அதனால இப்போ சரி பண்றோம்.
context: IT staff explaining to a manager.
explain: 'Secure' means safe from danger.
usage: Use it at work in IT updates and reports.
leelaQ: Why is a secure website important?
answer: It keeps people's information safe.

en: I have not checked my social media today.
tamil: நான் இன்னைக்கு என் சோஷியல் மீடியாவை பாக்கல.
context: Telling a friend about your day.
explain: 'Today' shows the day is not finished, so use present perfect.
usage: Use it in casual talk about screen time.
leelaQ: How often do you check social media?
answer: I check it a few times a day.

en: Do you think it is a good idea to buy a second-hand phone?
tamil: செகண்ட்-ஹேண்ட் போன் வாங்குறது நல்ல யோசனைன்னு நினைக்கிறியா?
context: Asking a friend for advice.
explain: 'Do you think...?' asks for an opinion.
usage: Ask a friend or a seller before you buy a used device.
leelaQ: What are the good points of a second-hand phone?
answer: It is cheaper, but the battery may be weak.

en: Where did you buy this laptop bag?
tamil: இந்த லேப்டாப் பேக்கை எங்க வாங்கின?
context: Asking a friend.
explain: 'Where did you buy...?' asks about a place in the past.
usage: Ask in casual talk about gadgets.
leelaQ: Where do you keep your laptop?
answer: I keep it in a bag on my study table.

en: Is there any shop nearby that repairs phones?
tamil: பக்கத்துல போன் ரிப்பேர் பண்ற கடை ஏதாவது இருக்கா?
context: Asking a local person.
explain: 'Is there any...?' asks if something exists nearby.
usage: Ask a local person or a security guard when your phone breaks in a new place.
leelaQ: How do you find a good repair shop?
answer: I ask my friends and read reviews online.

en: I just bought a new smart watch, and it tracks my steps.
tamil: நான் இப்போதான் ஒரு புது ஸ்மார்ட் வாட்ச் வாங்கினேன், அது என் நடையை கணக்கு வெக்குது.
context: Showing a friend a new gadget.
explain: 'Just' shows something happened a moment ago. 'Tracks' means keeps a record.
usage: Say it when you show off or explain a gadget.
leelaQ: Would you like to wear a smart watch?
answer: Yes, I would like one to count my steps.

en: The hotel Wi-Fi works well, but the signal is weak in the corridor.
tamil: ஹோட்டல் வைஃபை நல்லா வேலை செய்யுது, ஆனா காரிடார்ல சிக்னல் வீக்கா இருக்கு.
context: Giving feedback at a hotel desk.
explain: 'But' joins two opposite ideas.
usage: Say it at a hotel reception when giving feedback.
leelaQ: Do you check the Wi-Fi when you stay in a hotel?
answer: Yes, I always ask about the Wi-Fi before booking.

en: My brother is playing a game on the tablet right now.
tamil: என் தம்பி இப்போ டேப்லெட்ல கேம் விளையாடிட்டு இருக்கான்.
context: Telling a guest why the tablet is busy.
explain: 'Right now' stresses that it is happening at this moment.
usage: Use it in casual talk at home.
leelaQ: What games do you play on your phone?
answer: I play puzzle games when I have free time.

en: We got a new router yesterday, and the speed is much better.
tamil: நாங்க நேத்து புது ரூட்டர் வாங்கினோம், இப்போ ஸ்பீடு ரொம்ப நல்லா இருக்கு.
context: Sharing good news about the internet at home.
explain: 'Much better' is a comparison that shows a big change.
usage: Say it to neighbours or relatives who ask about internet.
leelaQ: How fast is your internet?
answer: It is quite fast, so I can watch videos without waiting.

en: I will update my phone tonight when I get home.
tamil: நான் இன்னைக்கு ராத்திரி வீட்டுக்கு போனதும் என் போனை அப்டேட் பண்ணுவேன்.
context: Planning a phone update.
explain: After 'when', use present simple even for the future.
usage: Say it when you decide to do a task later.
leelaQ: What will you do on your phone tonight?
answer: I will talk to my friends and watch a movie.

en: She has saved all my contact numbers on her new phone.
tamil: அவ என் எல்லா காண்டாக்ட் நம்பர்களையும் தன் புது போன்ல சேவ் பண்ணி வெச்சிருக்கா.
context: Talking about a sister or friend.
explain: 'Has saved' shows a finished action with a result now.
usage: Use it when you tell someone that your number is already with a person.
leelaQ: Do you remember phone numbers or save them?
answer: I save them because I cannot remember many numbers.

en: The speaker in this room has a loud echo.
tamil: இந்த ரூம்ல ஸ்பீக்கர்ல பெரிய எக்கோ வருது.
context: Telling the organiser about audio trouble.
explain: 'Echo' is the sound that repeats.
usage: Say it at a meeting room or a hall with sound problems.
leelaQ: Where have you heard a loud echo?
answer: I heard one in a big empty hall.

en: I usually pay my electricity bill through an app.
tamil: நான் பொதுவா என் கரண்ட் பில்லை ஆப் மூலமா கட்டுவேன்.
context: Telling a friend how you pay bills.
explain: 'Through' means by using something.
usage: Use it when you talk about easy online payments.
leelaQ: How do you pay your bills?
answer: I pay them on my phone using UPI.

en: I am waiting for the page to load.
tamil: நான் பேஜ் லோட் ஆகுறதுக்காக காத்துட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Telling someone why you are slow to respond.
explain: 'Waiting for' plus a noun and 'to' shows what you expect.
usage: Say it on a call or at a counter when a system is slow.
leelaQ: What do you do when a page loads slowly?
answer: I wait for a minute and then refresh it.
